Apprehending his arrest, petitioner- Sushant Kumar Gupta has moved this Court for grant of
anticipatory bail in connection with Rc Case No.67(S)/2017/EOW/ Ranchi registered under
Sections 420, 34, 120B, 409, 468, 471 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4, 5, 6 of Prize Chits
and Money Circulation (Banning) Act, 1978.

sentences.text: 2.  It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the original Dhanwar P.S. Case No.180/2014 is the basis of the present case in which the petitioner was not named as an accused.

3. It is further submitted that in another case being RC Case No. 7(S)/2016, which is founded on similar fact situation this petitioner has been enlarged on anticipatory bail being A.B.A. No. 4270 of 2019 after depositing Rs. 5 Lakh.
The present case is on the same footing and based on the same witnesses and same documents.

The provisional complaint was filed on the basis of which the present case has been registered on 03.08.2014, whereas this petitioner had submitted his resignation on 29.03.2012 which is the reflected in the charge sheet and also in support of it,
Form-32 has been filed.
During search and seizure operation, nothing has been seized from the possession of this petitioner or from his house.

After submitting his resignation when the petitioner got wind of the illegality being committed by the company, he filed Sanha No. 430 of 2014 stating therein that Sarfaraj Ansari, Chief Managing Director of the company namely, Amrit Ganga Agro Industries Ltd., was committing illegality.
Even after the resignation of the petitioner from the company, his scanned signature was used showing to be one of the Directors of the company.
However, Form 32 will not reflect any of his signatures.

sentences.text: 1 collection of the deposit from Raj Dhanwar which was very meagre and the total collection has been stated to be Rs.1,89,600/- in which the petitioner had no role to play.

However, there are conflicting version regarding the deposit received from the places and finally the Branch at Dhanwar had to be closed because there was no fund to be received, despite the amount has been deposited from the earlier case but no one has come up to receive the amount from the Court below.

4. Learned counsel for the CBI has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that the petitioner was the founder Director of the company along with Md. Sarfaraj Ansari (A-1) which was incorporated on 05.05.2011 and he played active role in the affairs of the company by signing redeemable preference share certificate issued to the investors as authorized signatory.

The total amount of Rs.40,30,402/- and Rs. 2,07,000/- were credited in the account of the company and the amount was withdrawn through cheques and also transferred/diverted to his personal account number lying with the Bank of India, Kahalgaon Branch, Bihar and in the saving bank account of his father.
5. The modus operandi to attract investment, was to give commission to the agents on it at a very high rate.
Minimum 18% to maximum 28% was given to the agents as spot commission.

In order to allure the investors, it was falsely projected that the Company was involved in business of bricks manufacturing, goatery division, dairy division etc.
6.

From the charge sheet, it will be manifest that total sum of Rs.14,97,000 has been transferred in the personal account of the petitioner from the account of the company apart from the cash collected from the branch office.

7. I find force in the submission made on behalf of the CBI that allegations are similar, but the offences are distinct in the present case vis-a-vis R.C. Case No.7(S)/ 2016 in which the petitioner has already been enlarged on bail on depositing Rs.5 lakhs.
Distinction in the offence is borne out by the distinct victims, place and the amount involved in both these cases.

Although the same company has been under investigation in both the cases, Distinctive features are as under:
I. R.C. Case No.07(S)/ 2016 was registered on the basis of Complaint Case No.
87/2013 filed by Zakir Ansari of District Jamtara.

The present case i.e. RC Case No.
67(S)/2017 is registered on the basis of Dhanwar PS Case No. 180/2014 under District Giridih by the complainant Kumidini Devi.

II. RC Case No.67(S)2017/EOW/ Ranchi and the earlier RC Case No.7(S)/2016 relating to two distinct offence while present case is related to Giridih District involving embezzlement of Rs.1,71,44,600/- whereas the later pertains to the offence committed in Jamtara involving embezzlement of Rs.20,51,300/-.
8. Considering the gravity of offence, direct involvement and active role of this petitioner, I am not inclined to enlarge the petitioner on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, his prayer for anticipatory bail is hereby rejected.
Petitioner is directed to surrender before the Court below within two weeks.
